text:
SQLite, WAL mode. 20 users on one server is well inside its range [assumed: write-light CRUD, not heavy concurrent writes]

| | SQLite | Postgres |
|---|---|---|
| ops | a file, nothing to run | service, users, auth, upgrades |
| backup | `sqlite3 app.db ".backup x.db"` or Litestream | `pg_dump` / WAL archiving |
| concurrency | many readers, **one writer at a time** | full MVCC, concurrent writers |
| latency | in-process, no network hop | socket round trip |
| features | JSON, FTS5, CTEs | + `LISTEN/NOTIFY`, rich types, extensions, row-level security |
| scale out | single host only | replicas, multiple app servers |

setup: `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000; PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON;` → writes queue briefly instead of failing with `SQLITE_BUSY`

pick Postgres if:
- a second app server or separate worker host is planned
- long write transactions or bulk imports run during working hours
- Postgres is already run and backed up elsewhere → near-zero marginal ops cost
- needs PG-only features: `LISTEN/NOTIFY`, PostGIS, RLS

migration later: low cost when access goes through an ORM or query builder and SQLite-only quirks are avoided (loose typing, `INSERT OR REPLACE`)
